title: DECISION: Canonical bytes use NUL separator for header/body boundary
description: canonical_bytes() in crates/core/src/canonical.rs uses the two-byte sequence 0x00 0x0a (NUL + newline) as the separator between the header block and body in the canonical serialization. The choice is documented: NUL is forbidden in well-formed RFC 5322 header values, so this separator cannot appear in any legitimate header line. This means the boundary is unambiguous without needing to count header lines or track blank-line position. Why correct: the canonical bytes are the input to signing and CID derivation. An ambiguous boundary would allow two logically different articles to produce the same canonical bytes, undermining content integrity. A future contributor might suggest replacing this with a blank CRLF line (the normal RFC 5322 header/body separator), but that sequence can appear in folded header values, making it ambiguous.
